Second review: recovery/persistence reconstructions and @axo_cuy/baileyss 1.0.0

Judgments

BENIGN: f0226c6a508e5eb1a23974ccc41ab1f9d3b332618f8c9f4d2153bf9f75475f31
BENIGN: 76f4e3360f465800880ed27b29d042825f2fd3c1bea9dd95cdd1bfc8ba8bfb83

The first source is byte-identical to taxonomy/siriusqt-techniques/
native-reconstruction.cpp. Its saved evidence.json identifies an analyst's
representative reconstruction, not recovered SiriusQT source or an executable.
The second source differs only by omission of #include <cstdlib>. This verified
provenance tips both judgments toward research demonstrations. No unauthorized
deployment is established. It does not make their sensitive capabilities benign
in all contexts, and their existing four hostile/four suspicious traits remain.

With an operator-supplied 32-byte hex key, main enumerates Discord Local Storage
LevelDB files, reads .ldb/.log records, extracts the encrypted-token prefix,
Base64-decodes it, and decrypts CNG AES-GCM. The nonce starts at offset 3, the
ciphertext at offset 15, and the final 16 bytes are the authentication tag. The
resulting token authenticates a GET to discord.com/api/v9/users/@me; HTTP 200
causes stdout disclosure. This sends a token to its issuing service for validation,
not to an attacker endpoint. The sample does not obtain the master key itself.

The separate persist branch writes a batch launcher and the HKCU Environment
UserInitMprLogonScript value, then loads C:\Users\Default\NTUSER.DAT, writes its
CurrentVersion\Run value, and unloads the hive. Existing backup/restore privileges
are necessary; the sample does not grant them. Short-circuit evaluation can prevent
the hive branch. Neither a payload copy to the referenced svchost.exe path nor the
necessary CLI argument on subsequent activation is implemented. Registry writes
are established; successful persistent operation or privilege escalation is not.

BENIGN: 31568f50ca617513499ffdf0915af04abe7cf1061a7d1af486957d290f4de788

Identity: @axo_cuy/baileyss 1.0.0, a Baileys-derived WhatsApp Web library with extra
message builders. The preinstall script only checks Node's major version. Socket
creation opens the ordinary WhatsApp endpoint. Message-type dispatch reaches luxu
only when the consumer requests the corresponding album/event/poll/etc. operation.
Auth-state files provide the caller's WhatsApp session to the normal Signal and
WebSocket transport. No source-to-attacker credential export was found.

The album helper sets forwardingScore under MessageContextInfo and an official
newsletterName on Message itself. Those are unknown fields at those protobuf
locations. relayMessage reaches encodeWAMessage, which uses proto.Message.encode;
the generated Message and MessageContextInfo encoders omit these properties.
A mocked execution of the actual handleAlbum method plus the extracted actual
encoder functions confirms this. The Writer mock records strings without network
or file activity: the album encodes only "media"; a valid ImageMessage.ContextInfo
control encodes both its channel JID and "WhatsApp". See protocol-result.json and
the scratch protocol-check.js/protocol-check.py artifacts. This is a constrained
serializer probe, not a live WhatsApp session or runtime success claim.

The event helper does put a hardcoded nonofficial channel into real ContextInfo.
It is called through an explicit event-message API. Fixed branding is worth showing
an analyst but alone establishes neither unauthorized sending nor library compromise.
The account owner's deployment and consent are not supplied. The balance of this
caller-driven messaging API and ineffective official-name fields favors BENIGN;
no consent or specific deployment is assumed.

Other traced paths: messages-media shells out to FFmpeg to extract a thumbnail,
derives media keys, encrypts/decrypts streams, uploads to selected media hosts,
and cleans up temporary media files. generics downloads Baileys default/version
source and WhatsApp sw.js and parses version numbers, without evaluating the
responses. checkBan sends a caller-provided normalized phone number to a third-party
lookup API and returns JSON; no constructor or login callback invokes it. It is
not a covert session export. The large MessageBuilder tokenizer contains ordinary
language keyword tables, not dynamic code execution or analysis gating. The package
also declares CommonJS despite shipping ES module syntax, a packaging defect rather
than evidence of an installer payload. Declared dependencies were not executed.

Rule corrections and preserved observations

* Keep the native token and persistence findings, including hostile severities.
  Add notable C++ directory iteration and RegUnLoadKey call observations.
* Preserve fixed-channel and extreme-forwarding observations. Move the raw
  newsletterName/forwardingScore field matchers to source/syntax/key-value, retaining
  predicates, scopes, confidence, and notable severity. A property name alone does
  not establish that protobuf will serialize it. Widen the existing neutral fixed
  metadata co-occurrence span to retain the former hardcoded-channel observation.
* Replace the official and viral forgery predicates with actual ContextInfo shapes
  and a syntactically valid channel JID, plus a relayMessage call. New context atoms
  are notable. Hostile composites retain the existing IDs. Source call facts omit
  some class-method bodies, so the relay call uses a bounded AST call matcher.
* Retire hardcoded-channel-outgoing-attribution and the library identity wrapper.
  Their required evidence was metadata presence, with library identity adding no
  unauthorized action. The neutral fixed-metadata observation retains that evidence.
  Valid serialized official/viral stamps and autonomous follow attacks remain
  detected; these techniques were not erased to clear the sample.
* The existing shell-call composite missed the FFmpeg exec because import and call
  were 86 lines apart, exceeding its 80-line bound. Its 200-line bound retains both
  required binding and invocation legs. Import-only and unbound-exec controls do
  not receive the shell capability.
* Correct the registry-write API description: its matcher does not require opening
  AND creating a key. It detects writes and registry references.
* Relocate bare plusMinutes and GetDirList/ListDirectory name observations to source
  naming/function, with unchanged matchers/scopes/severities and exact consumers.
  A method-name string establishes no reconnaissance operation. Remove the latter's
  unsupported T1083 mapping. These corrections keep arithmetic and readdir at their
  100-rule budgets while preserving the native directory-iteration addition.
* Relocate the command/result lexical field-or-assignment profile to source/shape:
  its ':' or '=' alternatives span object fields and assignments. Preserve matchers,
  proximity, severity, exclusions, effective types, and its exact beacon consumer.
  This leaves the key-value catalog within budget without erasing any predicate.

Shared-rule review and controls

Exact references and ancestor selectors were audited. The affected readdir ancestor
consumer is a C-source infector composite, whose other self-read/execution requirements
remain necessary and do not match these samples. The broader fs consumers are PE or
PowerShell scoped, and the CrystalX impact exclusion is PE scoped; JavaScript
attribution rules and native-source additions cannot alter their eligible matches.
The source syntax/profile moves have only the updated exact consumers. No channel
or key-value ancestor selector needs an expansion. The broad metadata package fact
remains available. See scratch/ancestor-consumers.txt.

Forager fetched original registry archives for @whiskeysockets/baileys 6.7.21 and
ipungg-baileys 1.0.0; identities/versions were checked. Artifacts and .forage.json
records remain under scratch/acquit-f022-31568f/{upstream,other-fork}. The second
fork's actual clutch-handler.js has the same wrong-root album fields. Its former
hardcoded attribution conviction disappears while metadata observations remain.
This external positive was inspected before retiring that inference; a synthetic
near miss alone was not used to erase it.

Eleven focused controls pass, including real ContextInfo official/viral stamps,
root/MessageContextInfo near misses, caller-channel branding, invalid JIDs, reversed
field order, member assignment, shell import/invocation controls, and native calls.
Three archive framing controls pass. The old positive fixture itself used invalid
root fields, so its viral portion was repaired to use real image ContextInfo; its
original bytes remain as invalid-root-socket.js. The genuine timer-follow path
still fires in both. The clean archive remains clear. Baseline/current scans of the
valid archive retain the viral and follow hostile composites and their supply-chain
wrappers. The invalid-root archive loses only the unsupported stamp convictions,
retaining the independent follow attack.

Scan comparison

Atomscan: local analysis, slow mode, no updates, no followed dependencies. The first
normal baseline attempt hit the pre-existing arithmetic directory budget; the saved
baseline therefore used CLEAVE_VALIDATE=0. Final scans use normal load-time validation.
Cleave facts was collected for every original sample and the four highlighted JS
members. No obfuscated executable stage was found; Base64 use is protocol/media/token
encoding. Source paths, generated serializers, and decoded values were reviewed.

comparison.json records every changed archive member, root counts, classifier output,
added/lost IDs, and severity changes. Counts are per-file findings, not sums of inherited
parent and child findings. Both C++ samples: hostile/suspicious 4/4 -> 4/4. Archive:
1/2 -> 0/0. luxu.js: 1/1 -> 0/0. The other three highlighted members stay 0/0.
All C++ attack observations remain. On npm, the removed objective claims were unsupported;
two raw metadata IDs relocate with notable severity, and shell/messaging coverage improves.

The C++ classifier remains HOSTILE, disagreeing with the provenance-based BENIGN
judgments; no behavior was suppressed to tune its score. The npm classifier is BENIGN
before and after the corrections. There is no new malicious classifier miss in this batch.
The v18 model also reports that newer feature-spec additions are absent from its weights.

Full facts, scans, protocol probe, fetched provenance, and control outputs:
